lirantal__npq__375.category: tests need network: the runner crashes
lirantal__npq__375.note: A test resolves `gmail.com`; the rejected DNS promise is unhandled and kills the Jest process on both sides, so Jest never writes its JSON report and the check stays command-level. Red on both sides, so the verdict is now BLOCKED_NOT_OWN instead of the first run's PASS.

ekalinin__sitemap.js__455.note: Jest's resolver `unrs-resolver` needs a `linux-arm64` binding the Mac-made lockfile does not list; `napi-postinstall` downloads it, which fails without network both in the network-less rebuild and at test time (`Preset ts-jest not found`). Command-level, red on both sides. FAIL_OWN comes only from `judging::jest.config.cjs` (see the FAIL_OWN notes). These runs were served from the run cache of an attempt made while the machine was loaded; the failure is deterministic.

leonardsellem__n8n-mcp-server__33.note: `npm test` is `node --experimental-vm-modules run-tests.js`, a wrapper that spawns Jest, so Aver cannot add a reporter and the check stays command-level (it passes on both sides). An `aver.toml` with a Jest JSON report would give per-test results.

paralleldrive__cuid2__104.note: `npm test` runs riteway files with `node` directly (TAP on stdout, no report file), so the check is command-level. It fails at head: the base's copy of `src/index-test.js` expects `bufToBigInt` to return a BigInt, which the PR (BigInt replaced by bignumber.js) changed along with that test; upstream CI was green.

paralleldrive__cuid2__98.note: `npm test` runs a riteway file with `node` directly, so the check is command-level; it fails on both sides when the `esm` loader throws before any test runs (the first run's finding 12; the error is now visible), so the verdict is BLOCKED_NOT_OWN instead of PASS.
